question: Under Warrant 1 Condition B in Table 4C-1, what are the 100-percent hourly volumes when the major street has two or more lanes and the minor street has one lane?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Condition B (Interruption of Continuous Traffic) of Table 4C-1, for a major street with two or more lanes and a minor street with one lane, the 100-percent (basic minimum) volumes are 900 vehicles per hour on the major street (total of both approaches) and 75 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach (one direction only). Warrant 1 is considered satisfied under Condition B if these volumes exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day. Standards (mandatory): - "These major-street and minor-street volumes shall be for the same 8 hours for each condition; however, the 8 hours that are selected for the Condition A analysis shall not be required to be the same 8 hours that are selected for the Condition B analysis." - The 100% column is defined by footnote a as the "Basic minimum hourly volume." Guidance (recommended): - "The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that one of the following conditions exist for each of any 8 hours of an average day: ... B. The vehicles per hour given in both of the 100 percent columns of Condition B in Table 4C-1 exist on the major street and the more critical minor-street approach, respectively, to the intersection." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 4C-1, Condition B, shows the row "2 or more" (Major Street) / "1" (Minor Street) with 100% values of 900 vph on the major street and 75 vph on the more critical minor-street approach. - [Image 3] The full-page view of Table 4C-1 confirms the same Condition B row values (900 and 75 vph at 100%). Citations: - Table 4C-1 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §5 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §112 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Guidance §4 (p.653) - Section 4C.02 Standard §56 (p.654)
gold_answer: 900 vehicles per hour on the major street, total of both approaches, and 75 vehicles per hour on the more critical minor-street approach in one direction.
